title: Base change and local descent for invariant symmetric-power lifting
statement:
For a commutative ring $A$ and a flat affine finitely presented group scheme $J$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $A[J]=\Gamma(J,\mathcal O_J)$. A rational $J$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with coaction $\rho:M\to M\otimes_A A[J]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities for the coordinate Hopf algebra; an invariant satisfies $\rho(m)=m\otimes1$, and an equivariant map commutes with coactions. Define $P(A,J)$ to mean that for every rational $J$-module $M$ and every equivariant surjection $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$ to the trivial module there are $n\geq1$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}_A^n M)^J$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q)=1$. Here $\operatorname{Sym}_A^n M$ is the degree-$n$ piece of the free commutative $A$-algebra on $M$, with its induced coaction and $\operatorname{Sym}_A^n A\simeq A$. No finiteness or flatness is assumed for $M$. Group schemes and homomorphisms use the group-object diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over the indicated affine base [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; affine, finite presentation, flatness, tensor product and symmetric algebra have the meanings of [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property, lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Let $H$ be such a group scheme over $A$. Then:
(1) For every ring homomorphism $A\to B$, $P(A,H)$ implies $P(B,H_B)$, where $H_B=H\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B$.
(2) If $A\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $P(B,H_B)$ implies $P(A,H)$.
(3) If $P(A_{\mathfrak m},H_{A_{\mathfrak m}})$ holds for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, then $P(A,H)$ holds; localization is as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
(4) If $\{\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A\}_{i\in I}$ is a finite jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $P(B_i,H_{B_i})$ holds for each $i$, then $P(A,H)$ holds. These assertions impose no Noetherian hypothesis on any base ring.

proof.text: Put $C=A[H]$. It is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. The base-changed group is again affine, flat and finitely presented, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], its coordinate Hopf algebra is $B\otimes_A C$, with structural maps obtained by tensoring those of $C$. For every rational module $T$, write $V_n(T)=\ker(\rho_n-u_n)$, where $u_n(x)=x\otimes1$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A T$. The symmetric-algebra base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] restricts to $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}^n_A T\simeq\operatorname{Sym}^n_B(B\otimes_A T)$: its map takes $b\otimes(t_1\cdots t_n)$ to $b(1\otimes t_1)\cdots(1\otimes t_n)$, and its inverse has the same degree-preserving formula. These formulas and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded] show compatibility with degree, evaluation and coactions, since both coactions are multiplicative and agree on every generator.

proof.text: To prove (1), let $N\twoheadrightarrow B$ be any rational $H_B$-module quotient $\lambda$. Regard it as a $C$-comodule over $A$, using $N\otimes_B(B\otimes_A C)=N\otimes_A C$, and put $E=\{(x,a)\in N\oplus A:\lambda(x)=a\cdot1_B\}$. This is the kernel of $\delta:N\oplus A\to B$, $(x,a)\mapsto\lambda(x)-a\cdot1_B$. Tensoring its kernel sequence with $C$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Consequently the two coactions on $N\oplus A$ restrict uniquely to $E\to E\otimes_A C$: their composite with $\delta\otimes1$ vanishes by equivariance of $\lambda$ and the trivial coactions on $A,B$. The counit identity follows by composing with $E\hookrightarrow N\oplus A$. Coassociativity follows by composing with $E\otimes C\otimes C\hookrightarrow(N\oplus A)\otimes C\otimes C$, which is injective by applying the same flat-exactness assertion twice. Thus $E$ is a rational $H$-module, its projections are equivariant, and $E\to A$ is surjective: for each $a$ choose $x$ with $\lambda(x)=a\cdot1_B$. No flatness of $B$ or $N$ is used.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat); agent fibre-product argument for Alper 9.3.1(i)

proof.text: Apply $P(A,H)$ to $E\twoheadrightarrow A$, obtaining $n>0$ and invariant $q\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_A E$ evaluating to $1$. The projection $E\to N$ followed by the degree-one inclusion into $\operatorname{Sym}_B N$ extends to an $A$-algebra map by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. It preserves degree by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. The two maps expressing equivariance agree on the degree-one generators and hence agree on the symmetric algebra by that universal property. Its image $q_B\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_B N$ is therefore $H_B$-invariant. Evaluation commutes with this map because it does so on $E$, where $\lambda(x)=a\cdot1_B$; hence $q_B$ evaluates to $1_B$. This proves (1).

For (2), fix $M\twoheadrightarrow A$ and put $V_n=V_n(M)$, $\epsilon_n:V_n\to A$ its evaluation. The scalar extension $B\otimes_A M\to B$ is surjective, since a chosen lift of $1_A$ gives lifts of every $b\in B$. As $B$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applied to $0\to V_n\to\operatorname{Sym}^n M\xrightarrow{\rho_n-u_n}\operatorname{Sym}^n M\otimes C$ identifies $B\otimes_A V_n$ with the invariants of the base-changed symmetric power, under the comparison in step 1. The hypothesis $P(B,H_B)$ therefore gives some $n>0$ for which $B\otimes_A\epsilon_n:B\otimes_A V_n\to B$ is surjective. The complex $V_n\xrightarrow{\epsilon_n}A\to0$ becomes exact after tensoring with $B$; faithful flatness, in the exactness-detecting definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], makes it exact already over $A$. Choose $q\in V_n$ with $\epsilon_n(q)=1$.

proof.text:
For (3), fix $M	woheadrightarrow A$ and keep $V_n,\epsilon_n$. Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak m$. For an $A$-module $P$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with $\ell_M=\mathrm{id}$ on $A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\ell_N:P	o P_{\mathfrak m}$, $p\mapsto p/1$, makes $A_{\mathfrak m}\otimes_AP	o P_{\mathfrak m}$, $(a/s)\otimes p\mapsto ap/s$, a localization at $S$; as $S$ already acts bijectively on the source, it is an isomorphism, natural in $P$. So step 1 with $B=A_{\mathfrak m}$ makes $M_{\mathfrak m}	woheadrightarrow A_{\mathfrak m}$ a rational $H_{A_{\mathfrak m}}$-module quotient, to which $P(A_{\mathfrak m},H_{A_{\mathfrak m}})$ applies. Localization exactness [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to the same kernel sequence, together with the degree-preserving comparison of step 1, identifies $(V_n)_{\mathfrak m}$ with $(\operatorname{Sym}^n_{A_{\mathfrak m}}M_{\mathfrak m})^{H_{A_{\mathfrak m}}}$. Evaluation is $q/s\mapsto\epsilon_n(q)/s$. A local lift of $1$ consequently has a representative $q/s$, with $q\in V_n$, $s

Let $I=\sum_{n>0}\operatorname{im}(\epsilon_n)$, an ideal of $A$. Step 5 says $I$ is contained in no maximal ideal, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives $I=A$. Thus choose a finite list $q_j\in V_{n_j}$, $n_j>0$, with $1=\sum_j a_j c_j$, where $c_j=\epsilon_{n_j}(q_j)$. If $A=0$, take $n=1,q=0$ and finish. Otherwise the list is nonempty. Let $n=\prod_j n_j$ and $k_j=n/n_j$. The elements $q_j^{k_j}$ are invariant and have degree $n$, by multiplicativity of the coaction and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. The ideal generated by $c_j^{k_j}$ is the unit ideal: a maximal ideal containing it would contain every $c_j$, contradicting $\sum_j a_jc_j=1$. Choose $b_j$ with $\sum_j b_jc_j^{k_j}=1$. Then $q=\sum_j b_jq_j^{k_j}\in V_n$ evaluates to $1$, proving (3).

proof.text: Fix $M\twoheadrightarrow A$. For each $i$, $P(B_i,H_{B_i})$ gives an invariant $q_i$ of degree $n_i>0$ in the symmetric algebra of $B_i\otimes_A M$ evaluating to $1$. Choose $n=\prod_i n_i>0$ and replace $q_i$ by $q_i^{n/n_i}$. Step 1 and the flat-kernel argument of step 4, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], identify these invariants with elements of $B_i\otimes_A V_n$ mapping to $1$. Because the family is finite, the explicit map $B\otimes_A V_n\to\prod_i(B_i\otimes_A V_n)$, $b\otimes v\mapsto(b_i\otimes v)_i$, is invertible: its inverse sums the maps induced by the coordinate inclusions $B_i\to B$ as $A$-modules. Assemble the $q_i$ to an element mapping to $1_B$. Exactness detection [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] for $V_n\to A\to0$ now supplies a global invariant of degree $n$ evaluating to $1$. If the family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $\operatorname{Spec}A$ empty, hence $A=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]; for $A=0$ the lift $n=1,q=0$ works. This proves (4).
